messages:
fintech_inc: Hey team — since ~07:12 UTC we're seeing a flood of 429s + intermittent auth timeouts hitting our Dedicated cluster in eu-west-2. p95 token latency went from ~120ms to ~1.6s. Also noticed a big billing jump for token usage. Is this an ongoing capacity problem on your side?

sam: Thanks for reporting. Really sorry. Can you paste a couple request IDs and a minimal curl repro? Escalating to SRE now — adding @lee.

fintech_inc: sample req ids: req_8a3c1, req_8b4d2. Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-dedicated-eu-west-2","input":"hi"}'
```
Responses: many 429 rate_limit_exceeded, some 504/read timeout. Clients retry -> duplicate consumption.

sam: Opening incident channel and tagging infra. @lee can you take a look at placement + autoscaler?

lee: looking. Initial telemetry shows repeated placement failures for the eu-west-2 dedicated pool between 07:09-07:18 UTC. Errors show PLACEMENT_NO_CAPACITY and ALLOC_THROTTLE. Autoscaler didn't trigger scale-up because group cooldown was active after a recent resize — looks like cooldown prevented emergency scaling. Also seeing a small subset of customers triggering noisy-tenant throttles which amplified contention.

anya: pulled runtime logs from the allocator. Confirmed allocation failures:
```
AllocationError: No capacity after 3 attempts, last_err=ALLOC_THROTTLE (node-pool eu-west-2-dedicated)
```
Fallback routing started sending ~10-15% of requests to eu-north-1 (policy 'regional-fallback'). That region has higher network egress times, hence the latency spike. Also observed short-lived token refreshes getting rejected during the switchover which caused auth errors.

marco: routing note: the 'regional-fallback' policy is configured to failover quickly when placement fails. In this case fallback_region=eu-north-1 which has slightly higher tail latencies. The billing spike seems tied to client retry loops: timeouts -> clients resend -> duplicate tokens billed. We should throttle retries at the gateway and advise clients.

sam: Proposed mitigations now: 1) temporary manual scale-up of eu-west-2 dedicated pool, 2) reduce autoscaler cooldown so emergency ops can scale, 3) temporarily relax regional-fallback aggressiveness. Can we action these?

lee: I'm manually forcing +4 instances into eu-west-2 now. Running orchestration command.

deploy-bot: autoscaler scale eu-west-2-dedicated --add 4 --reason "incident 1918012345 manual bump" queued by lee.

deploy-bot: New nodes provisioning. ETA ~6m.

anya: Pushing a small hotpatch to the placement controller to allow emergency scale requests to bypass cooldown. Patch diff uploaded to canary branch.

marco: I'm changing the routing policy to prefer local when degradation < 25% to avoid small perturbations causing full failover. Also messaging accounts to lower retry multiplier for affected clients.

fintech_inc: after ~8m the 429s mostly dropped. p95 latency improved but still around ~1.1s. Billing anomaly still shows elevated duplicate token charges — can you confirm a credit?

lee: confirmed allocation stabilized at 07:20 UTC. Current p95 ~180ms, 429 rate back to baseline. Creating follow-ups: SRE-4571 (fix cooldown logic to allow emergency scale), ENG-OPS-112 (improve routing visibility / metric alerts), CS-233 (billing reconciliation & potential customer credit).

sam: thanks all. We'll prepare a postmortem and update the runbook (add emergency scale procedure + routing thresholds). @marco please handle the customer comms.

marco: Drafting customer-facing summary and credit proposal for fintech_inc. Will share within 2 hours.

fintech_inc: appreciate the quick response. Please include the timeline and actions taken.

sam: incident resolved — moving to monitoring. Final note: keep an eye on noisy-tenant throttles and consider permanent limit adjustments to reduce blast radius. Last update 07:39 UTC.
